sources.name: Coin3D DIME repository and README
sources.evidence: DIME describes itself as a C++ DXF data-model library for loading, constructing, manipulating, writing, traversing, and extracting selected geometry. Its README declares the 3-clause BSD license.

sources.name: DIME feature and version notes
sources.evidence: The feature page says DIME was internally tested with DXF 10 through 14 and reports some customer use with AutoCAD 2000; these are not a broad future-version guarantee.

sources.name: DIME unknown-record API inventory
sources.evidence: Entity documentation says unhandled records are stored by the parent record holder. The class inventory includes unknown entity/object/table/class/section types. This supports a conditional tag-level preservation comparison, not exact byte or order preservation.

sources.name: DIME output API and release page
sources.evidence: The output API states that only ASCII DXF is currently supported despite a binary/DXB option. The release page lists dime-0.9.1 as the latest tagged release; published API documentation labels itself inconsistently as 0.9.1 and 1.10.0, so artifact provenance must be resolved before use.

sources.name: Open CASCADE Technology data-exchange overview
sources.evidence: The standard data-exchange list names open formats such as STEP, IGES, glTF, OBJ, VRML, and STL. The same overview places DXF and ACIS SAT under Advanced Data Exchange Components for proprietary formats.

sources.name: Open CASCADE Technology releases
sources.evidence: The current release list includes OCCT 8.0.1; no release evidence changes the official boundary that DXF and ACIS exchange are advanced/commercial components.

method.kind: Read-only internet primary-source review and local plan audit
method.limitations: DIME claims and documentation do not establish runtime compatibility for modern DXF versions or exact raw-byte preservation. Its release/source/documentation identity remains unresolved. OCCT documentation establishes product boundaries, not a qualified run of any commercial component. No peer or native runtime was installed or executed.

localCrosswalk.PAR-07/S8: DIME is optional only at the existing composed checkpoint for a still-open ASCII DXF unknown-record/tag-retention question. Bind exact source commit, artifact, compiler, and runtime; compare object identity, group-code/value sequence, owner/reference disposition, and strict reopen. Keep reconstructed tags distinct from byte-identical preservation.
localCrosswalk.encodingBoundary: DIME's published output API supports ASCII DXF only. Do not score Binary DXF, DXB-option claims, DWG, or unverified modern-version routes.
localCrosswalk.3dBoundary: Unknown ACIS/modeler carriers do not imply ACIS parsing or geometric semantics. Stock open-source OCCT is not an ACIS/DXF reader according to the official component inventory; separately licensed components are a different evidence route.
localCrosswalk.implementationCadence: No peer build or test is required during local fast slices. If a concrete comparison remains useful, run one source-pinned DIME control at the existing composed checkpoint using a generated-from-scratch temporary ASCII DXF; do not commit third-party drawings or add a dependency.
localCrosswalk.externalEvidence: J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain DEFERRED_EXTERNAL and non-promoting.
